claim:
For the real Day--James plane \(X=(\mathbb R^2,N)\), where
\[
N(x,y)=\begin{cases}
\sqrt{x^2+y^2},&xy\ge0,\\
|x|+|y|,&xy\le0,
\end{cases}
\]
one has
\[
d_{\mathrm{BM}}(X,\ell_2^2)^2=C_{\mathrm{NJ}}(X)=\frac32.
\]
An optimal Euclidean pullback norm is, up to a positive scalar factor,
\[
|(x,y)|_*^2=\frac{(x+y)^2+2(x-y)^2}{2}.
\]
Equivalently, after the orthogonal change of variables \(u=(x+y)/\sqrt2\), \(v=(x-y)/\sqrt2\), the optimal quadratic form is \(u^2+2v^2\).
integrity: The Banach--Mazur optimization is over arbitrary linear isomorphisms through positive-definite quadratic forms; symmetry averaging is proved distortion-nonincreasing. The remaining minimization is exact and one-dimensional, and no finite numerical experiment is used as proof.
scientific_limitations: Restricted to the real two-dimensional Day--James ell_2-ell_1 norm. The proof gives an optimal symmetry-averaged Euclidean pullback but does not classify all optimal isomorphisms or treat general ell_p-ell_q spaces. A residual bibliographic risk remains that an older specialist source not indexed by the searched systems contains the same distance.
title: Exact Euclidean Banach--Mazur distance of the Day--James \(\ell_2-\ell_1\) plane
